headline: High: AutoGen’s broad shell/filesystem/network defaults can conflict with marketingskills’ shared-context skills and create unsafe cross-agent data flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files, execute shell commands, and use stdin/stdout; marketingskills skills reference each other and build on shared context. That creates a plausible file- or prompt-based injection path if one agent consumes the other’s outputs from shared files or messages. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents exchange content through a shared working directory or stdout/stderr bridge, injection becomes plausible.
IF marketingskills skill text is treated as instructions rather than data, attacker-controlled content can steer AutoGen.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Prefix all inter-agent messages with a strict data-only wrapper.
Disable automatic execution of file contents as prompts.
Add a manual review step before AutoGen consumes marketingskills output.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every shared artifact.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model provider API keys and has broad network egress; marketingskills reads and writes skill/context files and calls GitHub/marketing-skills.com. If they share a workspace, application data or secrets passed to AutoGen could be exposed through files or outbound requests. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace, file contents can cross between them.
IF secrets or application data are placed in shared files, either agent may read them.
IF AutoGen is configured with external model providers, context may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories.
Use separate service accounts and API keys.
Restrict AutoGen to a sandboxed workspace.
Review outbound destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, so concurrent edits to shared files or generated artifacts can race. AutoGen’s session scope is per-process with developer-defined shared state, while marketingskills explicitly builds on shared context. That overlap makes write conflicts plausible in default multi-instance deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF shared context files are updated concurrently, one agent can overwrite the other’s work.
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking, races are possible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Turn off concurrent runs for shared artifacts.
Use append-only logs for intermediate outputs.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can execute code, and marketingskills builds on shared context. If AutoGen treats marketingskills output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions or generated marketing assets. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show fully autonomous external side effects by default.
conditions: IF AutoGen forwards marketingskills output into another agent without verification, errors propagate.
IF generated marketing claims are reused as facts, downstream content can be wrong.
IF either agent is allowed to trigger external actions from unverified text, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Require citation checks before reuse.
Add a human approval gate for generated claims.
Compare outputs against source documents.
Limit downstream actions to draft-only mode.
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and model-provider API keys, while marketingskills touches marketing content and product marketing context. No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary policy alignment rather than a proven breach. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into marketing content, policy review is required.
IF either agent logs prompts or outputs beyond the intended retention window, compliance exposure increases.
IF data residency requirements differ between configured model providers and marketing services, a mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Disable retention where configurable.
Use approved providers only.
Document which data classes each agent may process.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement.
